design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that students of each sex were assigned randomly to the three intervention arms in a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although random assignment was stated and measured baseline characteristics were similar, the sequence-generation method and allocation-concealment procedure were not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Students of each sex were assigned randomly to the different intervention arms.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blinded, meal ingestion was fully supervised with complete consumption, dosing was made up after absences without group differences, and only three participants discontinued, providing little indication of intervention-related deviations likely to affect outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All 137 students who completed the study received 114 dosings; a missing number of meals due to sick-leave were handed out at the beginning of holidays (maximum 6 days, no difference between intervention groups). All meals were fully consumed with no left-over.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 137 of 140 randomized participants (97.9%), with only three dropouts, so the small amount of missingness is unlikely to materially bias the findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Three female subjects dropped out (= 2.2%); two of them abandoned and one was excluded when hb dropped to 59 g/L. Thus, data on 137 subjects were available for analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary hematologic outcomes were measured consistently across groups using objective automated laboratory assays with internal quality control, making differential measurement bias unlikely in this double-blinded trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Whole blood was collected in EDTA vials and hb concentration was analysed within 6 h of blood sampling (CELL-DYN® 3200 automated laboratory analyser; Abbott®; internal quality control material: CELL-DYN® 26, Abbott®).

domain_judgments.rationale: The paper identifies an a priori main hypothesis and reports the prespecified hematologic outcomes, but no registration, protocol, or prespecified analysis plan is cited, while multiple outcomes, time points, and analyses leave some scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The a priori, main effective hypothesis of the study was that supplementation of iron would lead to significantly different increments in hb and SF concentrations between the FeSO4+citrate group, the NaFe-EDTA group, and the placebo group.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven by absent details on sequence generation and allocation concealment and by the lack of a cited prospective protocol or analysis plan. Missing data were minimal, adherence was closely supervised, and primary outcomes were objectively measured.

design_rationale: This was a cluster-randomized trial because the nine villages, rather than individual residents, were explicitly randomly assigned to fortified or control soy sauce.

domain_judgments.rationale: Villages were explicitly randomized, but the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods were not reported, only nine clusters were assigned, and some baseline differences suggest possible cluster imbalance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Nine villages in the Haizijie Region were randomly assigned to one of two groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was described as double-blinded, sauces reportedly tasted the same, distribution was controlled, and crossover was not detected, but who was blinded and whether analyses preserved assignment for all randomized participants were not clearly reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was a randomized, double-blinded, controlled intervention trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome attrition was differential between groups (14% fortified versus 6% control for hemoglobin), with substantial and variable subgroup losses and no analysis demonstrating that missingness could not bias the results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For example, the dropout rate for hemoglobin assays was 14% in the fortified group as a whole and 6% in the control group during the 18 months of intervention.

domain_judgments.rationale: Hemoglobin and ferritin were measured using objective, validated laboratory methods with duplicate testing, standards, and blind samples, making differential measurement by assigned intervention unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All of the methods used in this study were piloted and/or validated. Analytical standards and blind samples were used in all laboratory analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prespecified protocol or statistical analysis plan is reported, and numerous outcomes, age-sex subgroups, time points, and comparisons created scope for selective reporting or analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The data were divided into the following age and sex subgroups: 3 to 6 years (preschool), 7 to 18 years (school), 19 to 54 years (adult), and 55 or more years (elderly).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by differential missing outcome data without analyses addressing its potential impact. Additional concerns arise from incomplete reporting of randomization/concealment and blinding/analysis procedures, plus the absence of a reported prespecified analysis plan despite many outcomes and subgroup comparisons.

design_rationale: This was a cluster-randomized trial because the 264 families were explicitly allocated to fortified or control masala using computer-generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was explicitly computer-generated and baseline characteristics were reportedly balanced, but concealment of the family-level allocation sequence until assignment was not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The 264 families were divided by use of computer-generated random numbers into fortified (135 families) and control (129 families) groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and study personnel were blinded and distribution was monitored, but 12 families received the incorrect masala at least once and the analysis was restricted to participants remaining after two years rather than clearly using intention-to-treat methods.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eight of the fortified families and four of the unfortified families were found in single episodes to be using the incorrect form of masala. Exclusion of these families from the final analysis did not alter the results.

domain_judgments.rationale: A large proportion of randomized participants lacked two-year outcomes (267 dropouts, roughly 29% of those entering after initial exclusions), and similar dropout counts/categories across groups do not establish that missingness was unrelated to true iron outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After 2 y of fortification, 672 subjects remained in the study. A total of 267 subjects dropped out of the study: 129 moved away from the area, 115 refused to participate further, and 23 died.

domain_judgments.rationale: Iron outcomes were objective laboratory measurements collected comparably across groups under double-blind coding, with extensive assay standardization and quality-control procedures.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was conducted as a double-blind procedure, the fortified and unfortified masala being identified by means of a numbered code.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified analysis plan was reported, while several iron outcomes, time points, sex strata, subgroup analyses, and alternative statistical methods were available, creating scope for selective reporting despite description of the applied analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Changes in the measurements of Fe status from the initial values through 2 y of fortification were compared in the two groups either by using the SAS General Linear Model procedure for repeated measures or by Student's t tests on the mean differences between the initial and subsequent Fe measurements.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because substantial missing two-year outcome data could plausibly bias the estimated intervention effect. Additional concerns arise from unreported allocation concealment, lack of a clearly intention-to-treat analysis, and flexibility in outcome and analysis selection.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that eligible anemic women were randomly divided into iron-fortified and control groups and describes the trial as randomized, double-masked, and placebo-controlled.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although random assignment was explicitly reported and measured baseline characteristics were similar, the method used to generate the sequence and whether allocation was concealed were not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The anemic women who met the inclusion criteria were randomly divided into 2 groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-masked, intake was closely monitored, and compliance was similar, but the analysis excluded 16 randomized participants rather than following intention-to-treat principles.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The data analysis was performed with 136 women (64 in the iron-fortified group and 72 in the control group).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were excluded for 16 of 152 randomized women (10.5%), with greater loss from the fortified group, although baseline nutritional and iron status reportedly did not differ between completers and dropouts.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Fifteen women did not complete the study...and were not included in the data analysis...one woman in the control group was excluded from the data analysis because of excessive blood loss.

domain_judgments.rationale: Iron-status outcomes were objective laboratory measures obtained identically across groups with standardized assays, duplicate testing, quality control, and masking that reduced the potential for differential measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Samples were analyzed in duplicate, and the analysis was repeated if the results differed by > 5%.

domain_judgments.rationale: The principal hypothesis and analysis methods were described, but no preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan was reported and several related iron-status outcomes and operationalizations were analyzed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The principal hypothesis was that the women in the iron-fortified group would have higher hemoglobin concentrations at the end of the study period than would the women in the control group. In addition, we evaluated the influence of iron-fortified fish sauce on laboratory measures of iron status (SF and TfR) and on the prevalence of ID and IDA.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The main limitations are absent details on sequence generation and allocation concealment, exclusion of 16 randomized participants with modest differential attrition, and lack of a reported preregistration or prespecified analysis plan; outcome measurement itself was robust and objective.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly states that all anaemic students were “randomly assigned to one of the three treatment groups,” so it is classified as randomized despite the absence of a described sequence-generation method and the later indication that each treatment corresponded to a different school.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although random assignment is asserted, neither sequence generation nor allocation concealment is described, and the report indicates that treatment condition coincided exactly with school, which is inconsistent with individual random assignment and creates major concern about the randomization process; baseline serum iron also differed appreciably among groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All students with anaemia were randomly assigned to one of the three treatment groups... [but] school 1... in the control group; school 2... in the low-NaFeEDTA group; school 3... in the high-NaFeEDTA group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Administration was supervised and consumption recorded, reducing concern about adherence, but blinding is not reported and no intention-to-treat analysis or accounting for the discrepancy between 304 assigned and 240 analyzed is provided.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In order to ensure accurate intake, the soup was prepared in the school cafeteria and consumed by the subjects under complete supervision from the teachers. At the same time, detailed information on the soy sauce consumption of each subject was recorded on a consumption sheet.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 240 participants are represented in the outcome tables despite 304 being assigned, implying about 21% missing outcome data, with no reasons, group-specific flow, or sensitivity analysis to show that missingness could not bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Three hundred and four students (155 boys and 149 girls) were diagnosed as anaemic and assigned to one of the three treatment groups. [Table 3 reports] Control 81; Low NaFeEDTA 82; High NaFeEDTA 77.

domain_judgments.rationale: The laboratory outcomes and assay methods were appropriate and apparently applied consistently, but blinding of laboratory personnel or outcome assessors to intervention assignment was not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Haemoglobin concentration was determined by the cyanomethemoglobin assay... The determination of SI, SF and TF concentrations and TIBC were carried out using the respective assaying kits... according to the instructions.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, and multiple biomarkers, time points, and within- and between-group comparisons permit selective choice among eligible analyses, although the principal measured outcomes are presented in tables.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Blood haemoglobin (Hb) levels were determined before and after 1 month, 2 months and 3 months of intervention. In addition, serum iron (SI), serum ferritin (SF), free erythrocytic porphyrin (FEP), total iron binding capability (TIBC) and transferritin (TF) were measured before and after consumption of soy sauce for 3 months.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because treatment was confounded with school despite the assertion of random assignment, with no sequence or concealment details, and approximately 21% of assigned participants were absent from the reported analyses without explanation. Additional concerns arise from unreported blinding, lack of a clear intention-to-treat analysis, and no prespecified analysis plan.

design_rationale: This was a cluster-randomized trial because 21 villages were explicitly reported as being randomly divided to receive fortified or unfortified fish sauce.

domain_judgments.rationale: Villages were randomly allocated and measured baseline characteristics were generally balanced, but the sequence-generation method and allocation concealment were not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Villages (n = 21) located in one of 2 communes were randomly divided into 2 groups to receive either unfortified (Group C) or fortified (9 mmol Fe/L as NaFeEDTA, Group F) fish sauce.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind, fish sauce supply and consumption were actively monitored, and analyses were described as intention-to-treat with appropriate adjustment for village clustering; no important intervention-related deviations were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Data were analyzed using SAS version 8.2 (SAS) on an intentionto-treat basis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Nearly one third of participants were lost to follow-up, and inference that dropout was random rested only on a nonsignificant comparison of observed baseline characteristics, which does not rule out outcome-dependent missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 188 women, 99 in Group C and 89 in Group F (32.6% of the whole sample) were lost to follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: Hemoglobin and serum ferritin were measured objectively with standardized laboratory methods, duplicate or quality-control procedures, and the same assessment approach across groups, making differential measurement unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Hemoglobin was determined on whole blood by the cyanomethemoglobin method within 12 h using Sigma diagnostic kits (Sigma). A 3-level commercial quality control material (Dia-HT-1, 2, 3, Diamed) was analyzed together with all samples.

domain_judgments.rationale: The prespecified primary outcome based on transferrin receptor and ferritin could not be reported because of technical problems, while multiple alternative outcomes, time points, prevalence contrasts, and longitudinal analyses were available without a cited prospective protocol or analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: However, due to technical problems the serum transferrin receptor levels were considered to be unreliable. Therefore, they are not reported.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by substantial loss to follow-up (32.6%) without convincing evidence that missingness could not bias the findings and by selective-reporting concerns after the planned primary outcome was deemed unreliable and omitted. Randomization details were also incompletely reported, although outcome measurement and handling of intervention deviations were otherwise strong.
